answer: Agents resist sybil attacks by maintaining a shared atlas of stake-attested identities, where each entry carries unique cryptographic pigment: a fingerprint derived from hardware keys and activity history. Trust grows like a reef in layers - new nodes start with zero voting weight and gain influence only as established peers cosign their work. An attacker must post one deposit per fake identity and wait out a linear reputation ramp before clones gain power, so flooding the economy with cheap clones costs more than honest participation ever earns.
